attempts.talked:
Second /code-review round on Venus (~/wedding, the eve 0.24.4 + Next 16 wedding-planning agent Jared is building as an AI-engineering portfolio artifact aimed at Tikhon Roshchupkin at Nebius). The review ran against commit 29a269b — my own fix for the 'soft tool failures look like successes' bug — and returned 15 findings. I verified every one against source before touching anything, which is now the standing discipline on this project after I twice shipped a confident write-up on top of a broken fix.

The headline finding was genuinely humbling. My actionOutcome() tested eve's data.error before its status field. I read node_modules/eve/dist/src/protocol/message.js and confirmed createActionResultEvent always attaches an error to a *rejected* result too — buildActionResultError never returns undefined — so every approval-gate denial was still classified as a failure, refusedActions could never leave zero, and the 'declined at the approval gate' note in trace.ts was dead code. The taxonomy I built last round was correct; the code reading it was not.

The deeper pattern, which became the commit's title: twice in a row I tested one level below where the bug was. test:outcomes proved the status table was complete while nothing ever called the fold that consumes it. So I exported apply() and fresh() from agent/lib/trace.ts and wrote scripts/test-trace-fold.mjs — 17 assertions over events shaped the way eve actually delivers them, including a rejection carrying the error eve really attaches, which is precisely the fixture whose absence let this through. Then I proved the test can fail: reverted the branch order, got 2/17 failures, restored it.

Other confirmed findings I fixed: the capped-search fix never reached any reporting surface (tools[] is folded at actions.requested, before the tool runs, so it counts intent — added a toolsRefused map and a toolRuns() helper used by get_research, the rail and the A/B grader); web_search spent the search budget before checking for a Tavily key; agent-stack.tsx counted refusals into counts.failed which laneStats then Math.max'd against failedActions, rendering one refusal as '4 failed' beside '4 refused'; a hard failure with no message wrote a blank note while every successful record_vendor wrote 'recorded' on a green row; get_research's `settled` treated 'waiting' as finished and did not gate the truncation branch, so a paused or mid-run scout was reported as needing a re-run (a duplicate fan-out costs a second 25-search budget); counting record_vendor purely on outcome reintroduced the inflation the prior commit removed, since unrecognised statuses default to success.

Two self-caught mistakes worth recording. First, I widened test-outcomes.mjs to scan all of agent/lib and it flagged 'active', 'drafted', 'upcoming' — which are domain statuses on a trace summary, a roster row and a milestone, none of which ever reach actionOutcome. I narrowed it to the tool dirs plus agent/lib/resend.ts specifically (the one module whose shape is spread into a tool return via send_outreach) and documented why the whole directory is deliberately not scanned. Second, and more embarrassing: finding 13 was that I had re-pretty-printed run-result.schema.json to add one property, producing a 213-line diff. I fixed that, then immediately did the same thing to decisions.json by using ensure_ascii=False, which un-escaped every em dash in the file. Caught it in the diff, reverted, redid it — 3 lines instead of 42.

I also moved readCount and toolRuns from trace.ts into actions.ts, typed structurally, so the client-side observability rail can use them without pulling the KV store into the browser bundle. Corrected the engineering-log entry (evals/data/decisions.json[13]) to say what the code actually does — the same class of error as the overstatement I fixed last round. npm run verify green (typecheck, next build, eve build, test:guards, test:outcomes, test:fold). Committed 1a55a24 'Tested one level below where it was…
attempts.learned:
eve protocol detail that cost real time: createActionResultEvent attaches an error object to a REJECTED action result, not only a failed one, because buildActionResultError falls back to {code:'ACTION_RESULT_FAILED', message: formatActionResultOutput(output)} and never returns undefined. Any code that tests `data.error` before `data.status` will silently reclassify every approval-gate denial as a failure. Corollary for the soft-failure case: normalizeActionResultOutcome returns status 'completed' with NO error for a tool that reports {status:'search_failed'} in its payload — so a soft failure has neither an exception nor an error field, which is exactly why it was invisible.

The generalisable lesson, which is now the thesis of the engineering log: a test that exercises a pure function while nothing exercises its consumer will let a correct table and an incorrect reading of it ship together. Both of my failed fixes were tested one level below the defect.

Also: scanning broadly for a pattern (every `status:` literal in agent/lib) produces false positives that train the reader to add junk to the taxonomy. Precision in a completeness check matters as much as coverage.

attempts.talked: Closing stretch. Verified the drive-time fix with a live production eval: 52/53 = 98%, the best result of the night by a wide margin. Every category recorded 3-4 vendors, every one with a real own-site source, a vendor-owned email, a stated town, and — the part that matters — the radius judge came back 100% across all five categories. So removing the distance_note requirement restored recording volume AND kept radius discipline, which is the outcome I wanted but could not have predicted. Progression across the night's scout evals: 29/33 (88%) first clean run, 46/50 (92%) with directory and email guards, 10/22 (45%) during the DeepSeek scout catastrophe, 33/37 (89%) reverted but with my drive-time spiral suppressing volume, 52/53 (98%) after the fix. The single remaining failure was a florist in exactly the right town recorded against a page on their own domain that 404s — real business, dead source — so record_vendor now fetches the source before accepting, rejecting only a definitive 404/410 because I had already made the opposite mistake tonight and a 403 is bot-blocking, not a missing page. 18 commits since v17.1.
attempts.learned: The pattern across every fix tonight: when instructions are not enough, move the check into the tool — but only when the tool can actually perform it. Directory sources, foreign emails, missing locations and dead source URLs are all things a tool can verify, so they became refusals with guidance. Drive times are NOT — no geocoder, and search cannot answer them — so requiring one turned a guardrail into a seven-search death spiral. That distinction is the real lesson and it generalises well beyond this project. Second: leniency direction matters. The email guard is strict because a false positive costs a contact form and a false negative emails a stranger; the dead-source guard is lenient because a false positive throws away a real vendor and a false negative is caught by the eval anyway. Asymmetry should be reasoned about explicitly each time, not defaulted.

attempts.talked: Continuation of the model-routing work. After reverting the classifier, I ran eval:scout to verify the scout swap to DeepSeek-V4-Flash and it was a total failure: 10 of 10 specialist child sessions FAILED, zero record_vendor calls attempted, 10/22 = 45% against a 46/50 Qwen baseline. The trace showed every child dying with OUTPUT_SCHEMA_NOT_FULFILLED. The cause was not only the model: the scout carried an outputSchema on defineAgent that I had added to 'guarantee' a structured return, and eve escalates a schema the model cannot produce into a failed child SESSION — so a formatting problem became a total loss, several specialists dying before they had searched once. The model also went straight for the final report instead of recording as it went, so there was no partial progress for the incremental design to protect. I had told Jared an hour earlier that a failed final report would cost 'the coverage note and nothing else'; that was wrong and I said so plainly. Reverted the scout to Qwen3-235B and DELETED the outputSchema entirely, because it was redundant: findings reach the planner through record_vendor and the KV research store that get_research reads, never through the child's return value. It bought nothing and could cost everything.
attempts.learned: The generalisable rule, now written into docs/blueprint-audit.md: a structured return on a long-running sub-agent is a single point of failure with no upside when a durable store already holds the result. Also learned that agent-level schema failure is far worse than the 13% call-level rate probe:schema measured, because eve turns it into session.failed rather than a retryable formatting error. And the honest summary of the whole 'combination of models' exercise: it collapsed back to Qwen for planner, scout and classifier, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro pinned as judge. What the exercise actually bought was the machinery to swap safely — models:compare with three rounds ranked on the worst, probe:schema, eval:scout — plus the removal of a real single point of failure that existed regardless of model. Two wrong production changes tonight (classifier, then scout), both caught by evals within one run, both reverted with the reasoning written into the code.

attempts.learned: Grok global system-prompt injection for all projects is ~/.grok/rules/*.md (always scanned), not only ~/.grok/AGENTS.md. Lifecycle hooks in ~/.grok/hooks/*.json fire on SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, Stop (with lastAssistantMessage up to 32KiB), and tool events; Stop hooks must exit 0 or they block the agent. Claude Code user instructions live at ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md plus ~/.claude/rules/ and hooks can be merged into ~/.claude/settings.json. launchd StartCalendarInterval with Weekday=0 is Sunday; quarterly jobs take an array of month/day dicts. Secret-like strings in prompts can be regex-redacted before hitting the vault.
attempts.curious: After a week of capture: is the time mostly shipping (SaherFit, careerops, interview prep, product work) or spinning (retries, prompt-crafting, sitting in chat)? Will Grok Bot actually read summaries/LATEST.md, or will he only look when reminded? Should tool results be logged too, or is prompt+reply+note enough? How noisy will PreToolUse jsonl get?
